cards.claim: New evidence confirms the marriage between Stephen Ralph Cartwright and Elizabeth Helen Rutt.
cards.quote: LONDON, ENGLAND - In a stunning revelation that has sent shockwaves through the British aristocracy, new evidence has come to light confirming the long-suspected marriage between Stephen Ralph Cartwright, a prominent figure of the 19th century, and Elizabeth Helen Rutt, a member of the esteemed peerage. According to documents unearthed by a team of historians at the University of Oxford, Cartwright, who passed away in 1862, tied the knot with Rutt in a private ceremony in the late 1850s. The discovery has sparked widespread interest among historians and genealogists, who are hailing it as one of the most significant findings in recent years. "We've been pouring over archives and records for years, and finally, we have concrete proof of this union," said Dr. Emily Windsor, lead researcher on the project. "It's a game-changer for our understanding of the Cartwright and Rutt families, and sheds new light on the social dynamics of the time." The marriage, which was reportedly kept out of the public eye due to the couple's desire for privacy, has been confirmed through a series of letters and diaries belonging to Cartwright's closest confidants. One such letter, penned by Cartwright's sister, Lady Charlotte Cartwright, describes the wedding as a "beautiful, intimate affair" attended by only a handful of close friends and family members. Elizabeth Helen Rutt, a member of the peerage with a storied history dating back to the 17th century, brought a significant amount of wealth and influence to the union.
